descriptionPt: Domine os sons que mais causam sotaque e falhas de compreensão para brasileiros: th, finais -ed, /h/ vs /r/ e pares mínimos.
descriptionEn: Master the sounds most affected by Portuguese L1 interference: th, -ed endings, /h/ vs /r/, and minimal vowel pairs.

lessons.titlePt: Sons do TH e Finais -ed Sem Vogal Extra

cheatSheet.example: We figured out why the third request failed.

cheatSheet.meaningPt: trabalhar passo a passo até resolver
cheatSheet.example: They worked through both checklists before noon.
I double-checked the path before leaving the office.

payload.sentence: I thought they worked through both checklists before lunch.
payload.ipa: /aɪ θɔːt ðeɪ wɜːrkt θruː boʊθ ˈtʃɛklɪsts bɪˈfɔːr lʌntʃ/
payload.ptTranslation: Eu achei que eles tinham passado pelas duas listas de verificação antes do almoço.
payload.phoneticsTip: Em 'thought' e 'through', toque levemente a ponta da língua nos dentes superiores (/θ/) sem soltar um /t/. Em 'worked', termine seco em /kt/ sem acrescentar um 'i' no final.

payload.sentence: She figured out the third bug and shipped the fix right away.
payload.ipa: /ʃi ˈfɪɡjərd aʊt ðə θɜːrd bʌɡ ænd ʃɪpt ðə fɪks raɪt əˈweɪ/
payload.contextHint: Contando que uma colega encontrou o terceiro erro e publicou a correção na hora.
payload.connectedSpeechNote: 'figured out' liga como /ˈfɪɡjərd‿aʊt/; 'shipped the' reduz a pausa entre /pt/ e /ðə/.

payload.question: Tell me about three small tasks you finished yesterday and how you double-checked your work.
payload.ptContext: Responda em 2 a 3 frases usando verbos no passado (-ed) como 'worked', 'checked' ou 'finished' sem alongar a sílaba final.
expectedTopics: Mention at least two completed tasks in the past tense
Explain how you verified or double-checked the result
Use crisp -ed endings without an extra vowel
starterChips: Yesterday morning, I worked on...
After I finished that task, I double-checked...
It took me a moment to figure out...

payload.scenario: You finished reviewing a shared document with two teammates and noticed a small mistake in the third section.
payload.taskPrompt: Write a concise 2-3 sentence Slack message explaining what you checked and what you fixed.
starterChips: Hey team, I just double-checked...
I figured out why the third section...
Everything is updated and ready for...
payload.sampleAnswer: Hey team, I just double-checked our notes and figured out why the third section had old numbers. I fixed the table and checked the totals again, so we are ready for the meeting.

payload.persona: Alex, a friendly teammate reviewing a checklist with you before a client demo.
payload.scenario: You and Alex are confirming whether the presentation deck and test environment are ready for 2 PM.
payload.openingLine: Hey! Did you get a chance to go through the third slide and test the audio clip?
objectives: Confirm what you already checked using past tense verbs
Mention one small detail you had to figure out or fix
Ask Alex to double-check one final item before the demo
starterChips: Yes, I worked through the whole deck and...
I figured out a small issue with...
Could you double-check if...

descriptionPt: Pratique frases reais de daily standup, code review, arquitetura, prazos e incidentes de produção.
descriptionEn: Practice real-world phrases for daily standups, code reviews, architecture discussions, and incident updates.

cheatSheet.example: We narrowed the bug down to a stale cache entry.
Let's sync for five minutes so everyone is on the same page.
I'll reach out to the backend team if the endpoint still times out.

payload.sentence: I finished the migration yesterday, and now I'm narrowing down a flaky test.
payload.ipa: /aɪ ˈfɪnɪʃt ðə maɪˈɡreɪʃən ˈjɛstərdeɪ ænd naʊ aɪm ˈnæroʊɪŋ daʊn ə ˈfleɪki tɛst/
payload.ptTranslation: Eu terminei a migração ontem e agora estou isolando um teste intermitente.
payload.phoneticsTip: Pronuncie 'migration' com /aɪ/ claro na primeira sílaba e evite transformar 'test' em 'testi' com vogal extra no final.

payload.sentence: Before we merge this PR, let's make sure we're on the same page about edge cases.
payload.ipa: /bɪˈfɔːr wi mɜːrdʒ ðɪs piːˈɑːr lɛts meɪk ʃʊr wɪr ɑːn ðə seɪm peɪdʒ əˈbaʊt ɛdʒ ˈkeɪsɪz/
payload.contextHint: Sugestão educada durante um code review antes de aprovar o merge.
payload.connectedSpeechNote: 'make sure' soa quase contínuo (/meɪk ʃʊr/) e 'we're on' se junta em /wɪr‿ɑːn/.

payload.question: Give a quick 20-second daily standup update: what you shipped yesterday, today's focus, and any blocker.
payload.ptContext: Estruture em 3 frases curtas (ontem, hoje, bloqueio) com ritmo objetivo de standup.
expectedTopics: Current blocker or confirmation that nothing blocks you
starterChips: Yesterday I wrapped up...
Today I'm focusing on...
My only blocker right now is...

payload.scenario: Your pull request has been waiting for review since yesterday, and another task depends on it.
payload.taskPrompt: Write a polite Slack ping to a teammate asking for a review and offering a quick walkthrough if needed.
starterChips: Hey! Reaching out about PR #...
Just want to make sure we're on the same page...
Happy to do a 5-minute walkthrough if...
payload.sampleAnswer: Hey! Reaching out to see if you have 10 minutes to review PR #42 today. I added tests for the edge cases we discussed, and I'm happy to jump on a quick call so we're on the same page before merging.

payload.persona: Maya, Tech Lead facilitating the morning standup.
payload.scenario: You need help unblocking a failing staging build caused by an environment variable mismatch.
payload.openingLine: Morning! How is the authentication PR looking for today's release?
objectives: Share your progress since yesterday clearly
Explain the staging blocker without sounding vague
Ask Maya who you should reach out to for staging permissions
starterChips: The PR itself is ready, however...
I've narrowed the failure down to...
Should I reach out to DevOps or...

descriptionPt: Treine ritmo natural, pedidos educados e compreensão auditiva com cenários práticos do dia a dia.
descriptionEn: Build natural rhythm, polite requests, and listening fluency across everyday scenarios.

cheatSheet.example: Do you want to grab a coffee before the workshop starts?
Sorry, traffic is heavy and I'm running ten minutes late.

cheatSheet.meaningPt: poderia me ver / eu gostaria de pedir (educado e natural)
cheatSheet.example: Could I get a medium iced latte with oat milk, please?

payload.sentence: Could I get an iced oat latte and a toasted bagel, please?
payload.ipa: /kʊd aɪ ɡɛt æn aɪst oʊt ˈlɑːteɪ ænd ə ˈtoʊstɪd ˈbeɪɡəl pliːz/
payload.ptTranslation: Você poderia me ver um latte gelado com leite de aveia e um bagel tostado, por favor?
payload.phoneticsTip: Mantenha 'bagel' com /eɪ/ na primeira sílaba e atenção ao Dark L no final (/ˈbeɪɡəl/), evitando transformar o 'l' em 'u'.

payload.sentence: I'm running about ten minutes late — could we push our coffee back slightly?
payload.ipa: /aɪm ˈrʌnɪŋ əˈbaʊt tɛn ˈmɪnɪts leɪt kʊd wi pʊʃ ˈaʊər ˈkɔːfi bæk ˈslaɪtli/
payload.contextHint: Avisando um amigo com educação que você vai atrasar alguns minutos.
payload.connectedSpeechNote: 'running about' liga em /ˈrʌnɪŋ‿əˈbaʊt/ e 'push our' flui sem pausa forte.

payload.question: What do you usually order at a coffee shop or bakery, and when do you like to go there?
payload.ptContext: Pratique preferências cotidianas usando expressões naturais como 'usually grab' ou 'prefer'.
expectedTopics: Your usual drink or food order
Time of day or routine context
One preference (e.g., iced vs hot, less sugar)
starterChips: Whenever I grab a coffee, I usually order...
I prefer it with...
My favorite time to go is...

payload.scenario: Your train stopped for 10 minutes, and you're meeting a friend at a café at 3:00 PM.
payload.taskPrompt: Send a friendly 2-sentence text message letting them know you're running late and suggesting what to do.
starterChips: Hey! So sorry, I'm running about...
Feel free to grab a table and order...
Should we push our chat back by...
payload.sampleAnswer: Hey! So sorry, my train stopped and I'm running about ten minutes late. Feel free to grab a table and order first — I'll be there by 3:10!

payload.persona: Sam, a friendly barista at a busy neighborhood café.
payload.scenario: You are ordering a drink and pastry for dine-in, and the barista asks about milk options and allergies.
payload.openingLine: Hi there! What can I get started for you today — for here or to go?
objectives: Order a customized drink politely using 'Could I get...'
Specify whether your order is for here or to go
Confirm one detail such as milk type or receipt
starterChips: Hi! For here, please. Could I get...
Do you have oat milk or...
Could you also warm up...

descriptionPt: Resolva check-in, imigração, conexões atrasadas e solicitações de hospedagem com naturalidade.
descriptionEn: Handle check-in, customs, missed connections, and hotel requests with confidence.

cheatSheet.example: Please keep your boarding pass handy at the transfer desk.
Because of the storm, several passengers had a missed connection.

cheatSheet.meaningPt: me colocar na lista de espera de um voo anterior
cheatSheet.example: Could you put me on standby for the 4 PM flight?

payload.sentence: My connecting flight was delayed, so I'm worried I might miss my boarding window.
payload.ipa: /maɪ kəˈnɛktɪŋ flaɪt wʌz dɪˈleɪd soʊ aɪm ˈwɜːrid aɪ maɪt mɪs maɪ ˈbɔːrdɪŋ ˈwɪndoʊ/
payload.ptTranslation: Meu voo de conexão atrasou, então estou preocupado de perder a janela de embarque.
payload.phoneticsTip: Em 'worried', evite pronunciar um /r/ forte como no português caipira; faça o som central americano /ˈwɜːrid/.

payload.sentence: Could you check if there's an earlier seat available or put me on standby?
payload.ipa: /kʊd juː tʃɛk ɪf ðɛrz æn ˈɜːrliər siːt əˈveɪləbəl ɔːr pʊt mi ɑːn ˈstændbaɪ/
payload.contextHint: Pergunta objetiva no balcão da companhia aérea tentando embarcar antes.
payload.connectedSpeechNote: 'Could you' frequentemente reduz para /kʊdʒə/ em fala rápida; 'seat available' junta /t‿ə/.

payload.question: What steps would you take first if your international flight got delayed by three hours?
payload.ptContext: Explique em 2 a 3 frases o que você verificaria primeiro (conexão, hotel, mensagem para quem vai te buscar).
expectedTopics: Checking the connecting flight or airline counter
Notifying hotel, host, or pickup contact
Asking about rebooking or meal vouchers
starterChips: The first thing I would do is...
Next, I'd reach out to...
If I missed my connection, I would ask...

payload.scenario: Your flight landed two hours late, so you will arrive at your hotel after midnight.
payload.taskPrompt: Write a short message to the hotel front desk asking them to keep your reservation active and confirm late check-in.
starterChips: Hello, my flight into town was delayed...
I expect to arrive around...
Could you please keep my reservation active for...
payload.sampleAnswer: Hello, my flight was delayed by two hours, so I now expect to arrive around 12:30 AM. Could you please confirm late check-in and keep my reservation active under Marcus Silva? Thank you!

payload.persona: Elena, an airline customer service agent at the transfer counter.
payload.scenario: Your first leg arrived late and you missed your flight to London. You need the next flight and want to know what happens to your checked bag.
payload.openingLine: Good afternoon, I see your flight just arrived late. May I scan your boarding pass so we can check rebooking options?
objectives: Explain clearly that you had a missed connection
Ask for the next available seat or standby option
Confirm whether your checked luggage transfers automatically
starterChips: Yes, here is my boarding pass. Unfortunately...
What is the earliest flight with...
Will my checked bag transfer automatically to...

descriptionPt: Estruture respostas com método STAR, explique decisões técnicas e demonstre ownership em inglês.
descriptionEn: Structure STAR interview answers, explain technical decisions, and show ownership in English.

lessons.titleEn: Explaining Impact with the STAR Method

cheatSheet.example: Database lock contention was the main bottleneck during checkout.
I took ownership of profiling the API and documenting the fix.
Let me walk you through the root cause and the metrics afterward.
The index change had a measurable impact, cutting latency by 45%.

payload.sentence: When we noticed a database bottleneck, I took ownership of profiling the slowest queries.
payload.ipa: /wɛn wi ˈnoʊtɪst ə ˈdeɪtəbeɪs ˈbɑːtəlˌnɛk aɪ tʊk ˈoʊnərʃɪp ʌv ˈproʊfaɪlɪŋ ðə ˈsloʊɪst ˈkwɪriz/
payload.ptTranslation: Quando percebemos um gargalo no banco de dados, assumi a responsabilidade de analisar as queries mais lentas.
payload.phoneticsTip: Atenção em 'noticed' (/ˈnoʊtɪst/, sem som extra depois do 't') e na sílaba tônica inicial de 'database' (/ˈdeɪtəbeɪs/).

payload.sentence: Walking stakeholders through the root cause helped us avoid rolling back the whole release.
payload.ipa: /ˈwɔːkɪŋ ˈsteɪkhoʊldərz θruː ðə ruːt kɔːz hɛlpt ʌs əˈvɔɪd ˈroʊlɪŋ bæk ðə hoʊl rɪˈliːs/
payload.contextHint: Mostrando maturidade técnica ao explicar a causa raiz em vez de apenas desfazer o deploy.
payload.connectedSpeechNote: 'root cause' tem foco tônico forte nas duas palavras; 'helped us' liga em /hɛlpt‿ʌs/.

payload.question: Tell me about a tough bug or performance issue you solved recently and its measurable impact.
payload.ptContext: Use a estrutura STAR (Situação, Ação sua e Resultado em métricas) mantendo foco em o que VOCÊ fez.
expectedTopics: Specific action and ownership you took
starterChips: In my previous project, we ran into a bottleneck where...
I took ownership of investigating it by...
As a measurable impact, we reduced...

payload.scenario: After a behavioral interview, you want to send a brief follow-up email reinforcing your enthusiasm and clarifying one architecture point.
payload.taskPrompt: Write a 3-4 sentence follow-up email thanking the interviewer and briefly highlighting your relevant experience.
starterChips: Thank you for taking the time to walk me through...
I especially enjoyed discussing how your team...
Where I've delivered measurable impact is...
payload.sampleAnswer: Hi Jordan, thank you for taking the time to walk me through the team's roadmap today. I enjoyed discussing how your platform handles high-throughput jobs, as taking ownership of queue bottlenecks was where I delivered the biggest measurable impact in my last role. Looking forward to the next steps!

payload.persona: Jordan, Senior Engineering Manager interviewing you for a Full-Stack Engineer role.
payload.scenario: Behavioral deep-dive on how you investigate production bugs and collaborate across teams.
payload.openingLine: Thanks for joining! To start off, could you walk me through a technical challenge where you had to take ownership under a tight deadline?
objectives: Set the context and explain why the issue mattered
Describe concrete steps you personally executed
State a measurable impact or post-mortem improvement
starterChips: Sure — last quarter we hit a bottleneck when...
To narrow down the root cause, I...
The measurable impact was that...

descriptionPt: Debata escalabilidade, latência vs consistência e pontos únicos de falha com vocabulário executivo C1.
descriptionEn: Debate scalability, latency vs consistency, and failure resilience with C1 engineering nuance.

cheatSheet.meaningPt: equilíbrio entre vantagens e desvantagens de uma escolha
cheatSheet.example: Storing denormalized summaries improves reads, with the trade-off of extra sync logic.
A single un-replicated auth service becomes a single point of failure.

cheatSheet.meaningPt: degradação controlada sem derrubar o fluxo principal
cheatSheet.example: We baked graceful degradation into recommendations so checkout stays fast.

cheatSheet.meaningPt: retornos decrescentes diante de complexidade adicional
cheatSheet.example: Splitting into twenty microservices right now hits diminishing returns.

payload.sentence: Adding a distributed cache slashes read latency, though the trade-off is eventual consistency.
payload.ipa: /ˈædɪŋ ə dɪˈstrɪbjuːtɪd kætʃ ˈslæʃɪz riːd ˈleɪtənsi ðoʊ ðə ˈtreɪd ɔːf ɪz ɪˈvɛntʃuəl kənˈsɪstənsi/
payload.ptTranslation: Adicionar um cache distribuído reduz drasticamente a latência de leitura, embora o trade-off seja a consistência eventual.
payload.phoneticsTip: Pronuncie 'cache' como /kætʃ/ ou /kæʃ/ (nunca 'cachê' em duas sílabas) e mantenha 'though' bem suave com /ðoʊ/.

payload.sentence: If we bake graceful degradation into the gateway, one downstream outage won't trigger cascading failures.
payload.ipa: /ɪf wi beɪk ˈɡreɪsfəl ˌdɛɡrəˈdeɪʃən ˈɪntuː ðə ˈɡeɪtweɪ wʌn ˈdaʊnstriːm ˈaʊtɪdʒ woʊnt ˈtrɪɡər kæsˈkeɪdɪŋ ˈfeɪljərz/
payload.contextHint: Defendendo resiliência arquitetural durante uma revisão de RFC.
payload.connectedSpeechNote: 'bake graceful' exige pausa curta para não embolar o /k/; 'won't trigger' usa parada glotal sutil no 't'.

payload.question: When choosing between strong consistency and lower read latency, how do you decide which trade-off fits the product?
payload.ptContext: Apresente critérios práticos (ex.: fluxo financeiro vs feed/analytics) usando linguagem analítica C1.
expectedTopics: Example where strong consistency is non-negotiable
Example where eventual consistency + caching shines
starterChips: It largely hinges on the domain: for billing or inventory...
By contrast, on read-heavy dashboards the trade-off...
Beyond latency, we also have to weigh...

payload.scenario: A teammate proposed introducing Redis cluster caching and Kafka event invalidation for an internal admin tool with 200 users.
payload.taskPrompt: Write a concise, diplomatic RFC comment pushing back on complexity and suggesting a simpler alternative.
starterChips: I appreciate the scalability angle here, though at 200 internal users...
Introducing both Redis and Kafka might hit diminishing returns because...
As a simpler trade-off, could we start with...
payload.sampleAnswer: I appreciate thinking ahead on latency, though for 200 internal users introducing both Redis clustering and Kafka invalidation feels like diminishing returns. We'd add two new moving parts — and potential single points of failure — just to shave off a few milliseconds. As a pragmatic trade-off, let's index the reporting view first and revisit distributed caching only if p95 latency crosses 300ms.

payload.persona: Priya, Staff Engineer challenging your architecture proposal during a System Design review.
payload.scenario: You proposed putting an in-memory cache in front of user permissions, and Priya questions stale authorization risks.
payload.openingLine: Caching permission lookups definitely cuts database load, but what happens if a user's access is revoked and the cache serves stale roles for five minutes?
objectives: Acknowledge the security trade-off directly without being defensive
Propose a concrete mitigation (short TTL, explicit invalidation event, or split critical vs non-critical checks)
Explain how graceful degradation works if the cache layer fails
starterChips: That's a fair concern — stale revocations are unacceptable, so...
We can mitigate that trade-off by...
If the cache layer degrades, requests should...
